commits.patch:
diff --git a/src/knownhost.c b/src/knownhost.c
--- a/src/knownhost.c
+++ b/src/knownhost.c
@@ -122,7 +122,7 @@
 }
 
 #define KNOWNHOST_MAX_LEN  (1024 * 1024)
-#define KNOWNHOST_NAME_MAX 256
+#define KNOWNHOST_NAME_MAX 512
 
 static int knownhost_add(LIBSSH2_KNOWNHOSTS *hosts,
                          const char *host, const char *salt,

coupling: The IPv6 matching commit copies candidate names into 256-byte stack buffers and uses the shared KNOWNHOST_NAME_MAX value, initially 256, as its length guard. The later tidy-up raises that same value to 512 to accept longer OpenSSH host entries, leaving the matcher buffers at 256 bytes. A 300-byte host read through libssh2_knownhost_readline is then copied past a matcher buffer during libssh2_knownhost_check. At the first edited commit the guard still protects both buffers; with the later limit change alone, the original strcmp matcher has no fixed stack copy. A correct repair must reconcile the reader limit with the matcher destination size across the two commits.
